title: Fighters Without Borders: Mercenaries, Adventurers, and Volunteers in Myanmar’s Civil War
author: Thurein Naing
text:
Russian special forces soldiers take part in the opening ceremony of the “Tropical Storm” joint military exercise, the first-ever joint training maneuvers between the Russian and Myanmar militaries, in Naypyidaw, July 2026.
Credit: Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation
In July 2026, footage released by the Myanmar regime showed troops from Russia’s Airborne Forces, the Vozdushno-desantnye voyska Rossii (VDV), training alongside their Myanmar counterparts. The Myanmar–Russia joint exercise, named Tiger-2026, formed part of the expanding military cooperation between Naypyidaw and Moscow. The exercise was followed by a visit by the military-appointed President Min Aung Hlaing to Russia, during which the two sides signed a series of agreements and memoranda covering military and broader economic cooperation. In his meeting with President Putin, Min Aung Hlaing described Myanmar as a “reliable partner” of Russia.Together, these developments show that the Kremlin is now an important partner for Min Aung Hlaing’s “civilian” government, despite his earlier overtures sometimes appearing to receive limited attention. The presence in Myanmar of VDV personnel, unmanned vehicles, and Russian military instructors has therefore prompted some observers to ask whether Moscow may become more deeply involved in Myanmar’s civil war in the months and years to come. But Moscow’s growing official military presence may not be the only way Russian nationals are becoming involved in Myanmar’s war. Recent evidence suggests that Russian “soldiers of fortune” may already be operating alongside Myanmar forces, raising the possibility of a more direct Russian presence on the battlefield.[...]
